_about: The 19 Key Questions to Explore Through Stories (What / Why / Who / Where / When / How) with the coding vocabulary used in the October 2026 reports. The MEL team may reword or switch off a question in the settings workbook; new tags and new questions need a developer, so that numbers stay comparable between batches.

status.clear: The story answers the question directly, with specifics.
status.partial: The story answers in part, in general words, or with a stock phrase.
status.not_stated: The story says nothing that answers it.
status.not_applicable: The question does not fit this kind of story (use only for individual-support stories, such as a kit given to one person).

voice.writer: The answer is the writer's own telling.
voice.community_quoted: The answer is in the words of a resident, inside quotation marks.
voice.community_reported: The answer is a resident's or a group's view, told by the writer ('they said that ...').
voice.official_quoted: The answer is in the words of an office-holder or staff member (for example a head teacher), inside quotation marks.

global_rules: A stock phrase such as 'everyone decided together' (सभी ने मिलकर निर्णय लिया) is partial, never clear.
Gender comes only from the text's own words or grammar, never from a name.
Household tools alone are partial for q01 and q15.
Daily care of a kitchen garden is partial for q19.
Every evidence span is an exact copy of story text (at most 3 spans per question); no span, no 'clear' or 'partial'.
The answer is one or two plain English sentences; say what is missing when the answer is partial.
Where a question rests on a field already coded (participants, dates, location, kit, maintenance), the Key Question answer must agree with it.

questions.short: What was done, and what shaped it
questions.text: What did the community do? What local resources, knowledge, skills, wisdom, or past experiences shaped the way it was done?
questions.prompt: What did the community do, and which local tools, skills, knowledge or past experience shaped how it was done?

questions.text: Why did the community choose to take up this activity? What need, challenge, opportunity, or aspiration led them to this decision? What alternatives were considered, if any?
questions.prompt: Why did people choose this work? What problem or hope led to it, and what else did they consider?

questions.text: Why did communities drop other activities / priorities?
questions.prompt: Were other needs raised and set aside? Which, and why?

questions.short: Who took part, in what roles
questions.text: Who is involved? Who from the community participates in the process, and what roles do they play?
questions.prompt: Who took part, and what did each group do?

questions.text: Who makes the decisions? Who takes the lead in identifying, prioritising, and deciding the activities to be undertaken?
questions.prompt: Who first suggested the work, and who decided?

questions.text: Whose participation is represented? How are women, men, and other community groups involved in the process? Are women actively participating in decision-making?
questions.prompt: How many women and how many men took part, and did women take part in the decision?

questions.text: Is participation inclusive? Are people from different social, economic, caste, age, disability, or other backgrounds participating? In particular, are women from different social backgrounds equally represented and able to influence decisions?
questions.prompt: Which groups (by income, community, age, ability) took part, and who was left out?

questions.text: Where did community members come together to discuss and decide on the activity?
questions.prompt: Where did people meet to decide?
Where exactly was the work done (site, hamlet, ward)?

questions.text: Where did the need/problem emerge? Where was the issue or need identified? Was it specific to a particular location or community? What was unique about the local context?
questions.prompt: Where did the need come from, and what is special about this place?

questions.text: Where were the resources, materials, or support sourced from?
questions.prompt: Where did tools, materials and help come from, and what did families receive?

questions.short: When it began, and why then
questions.text: When did the activity begin? Was the timing influenced by seasons, festivals, agricultural cycles, school calendars, disasters, or other local factors?
questions.prompt: When did the work start, and why then (season, festival, school calendar)?

questions.text: When did different community members begin participating?
questions.prompt: Did everyone join at the start, or did people join later, and why?

questions.text: How did the community reach decisions? How were different opinions or disagreements handled?
questions.prompt: How did people decide, and how were disagreements handled?

questions.text: How were local materials, skills, knowledge, or traditional practices incorporated?
questions.prompt: Which local materials, skills or traditional practices were used?

questions.text: How did the community respond to challenges during the intervention?
questions.prompt: What went wrong or was hard during the work, and how did people respond?

questions.text: How did community members, local institutions, leaders, or other stakeholders work together?
questions.prompt: Who worked together (leaders, institutions, neighbouring villages), and how?

questions.text: How did the activity address the identified need or problem?
questions.prompt: How did the work meet the need? What changed, with one number and a date?

questions.text: How will the community take ownership of and manage the asset?
questions.prompt: Who will look after it, and how?
